_comment: Technique records. evidenceCategory says what backs each one: 'teacher pedagogy' and 'research-informed' cite a source that genuinely addresses the technique; 'app heuristic' means PracticeMap chose it and no source is claimed. Triggers are evaluated against features actually read from the notation -- never against a rating alone.

techniques.title: Complementary rhythms
techniques.fits: A run of equal-duration notes, where the difficulty is coordination between consecutive notes rather than any single one.
steps: Play the group written, slowly enough that every note speaks.
Now play it long-short: hold the first note of each pair and hurry the second. The pair still lasts exactly as long as it does on the page, so the beat does not move.
Play it short-long: the reverse. Each transition that was comfortable one way is exposed the other way.
Alternate the two patterns, then start the long-short pattern one note later so a different pair of notes is joined.
Return to the written even rhythm, with the written articulation, at the pace you began.
listeningGoals: Pitch stays accurate when the finger has less time to arrive
The short note is genuinely short, not merely earlier
The bow stays in the string through the fast note
No tightening in the left hand between pairs
techniques.tempoRule: Start where the written rhythm is already clean. The rhythm variants make the passage harder, not easier, so they belong at a tempo you already own.
techniques.successCriteria: Both patterns feel equally comfortable, and the written rhythm afterwards feels easier than when you started.
techniques.returnToContext: Play the whole phrase written, then continue into the first note of the next phrase so the join is rehearsed too.
cautions: This changes the written rhythm on purpose and is a practice transformation, not an edition.

techniques.title: Count the subdivision, then play it
techniques.fits: Mixed note values or off-beat placement, where the demand is knowing where the beat is rather than moving the fingers fast.
steps: Find the smallest note value in the passage and say it out loud, evenly, without the instrument.
Keep saying it and add the written rhythm by tapping, so the fast pulse continues underneath the long notes.
Play the passage while still hearing that pulse; let the long notes be measured against it rather than felt.
Drop the counting and keep the same placement.
listeningGoals: Long notes last their full value and do not shorten into the next entry
Off-beat notes arrive late enough, which is usually the problem, rather than early
The pulse does not speed up during the easier bars
techniques.tempoRule: Slow enough that the smallest value is comfortably countable out loud.
techniques.successCriteria: You can start the passage from any beat and place the following note correctly without restarting the count.
techniques.returnToContext: Play the phrase from its beginning so the passage is re-entered in tempo rather than from a standing start.
cautions: PracticeMap chose this technique; no source here establishes it.

techniques.title: Slow practice with one stated goal
techniques.fits: A passage carrying several demands at once, where playing it slowly without deciding what to listen for tends to rehearse everything vaguely.
steps: Choose one thing to listen for, and only one. On this passage the first candidate is named above.
Play the passage slowly enough to hear that one thing, ignoring the rest for now.
Repeat, changing only that one element, until it is reliable.
Choose the next goal and repeat. Do not try to fix two at once.
Play at your normal pace and check whether the goal survived the change of speed.
listeningGoals: The one thing you chose, judged honestly
Whether it still holds when the tempo returns
techniques.tempoRule: Slow is defined by the goal: slow enough to hear what you chose to fix, and no slower.
techniques.successCriteria: The chosen element holds at your normal pace, not only at the slow one.
techniques.returnToContext: Return to the written tempo and articulation and play the phrase whole.
cautions: S03 supports having a purpose for slow practice and notes that slow and fast playing can differ. It does not establish a starting tempo or an increment; those numbers are PracticeMap's.

techniques.title: Loop the hard join
techniques.fits: One measure clearly harder than its neighbours, where the trouble is usually getting into and out of it rather than the measure itself.
steps: Take the last note before the hard measure and the first two notes inside it. That is the whole exercise.
Play just those notes, stopping cleanly, until the join is reliable.
Do the same at the other end: the last notes of the hard measure into the first note after it.
Join the two fragments and play the hard measure with one note on each side.
Play the phrase whole and notice whether the difficulty moved somewhere else.
listeningGoals: The note before the hard measure keeps its full value instead of being clipped in preparation
The first note inside the hard measure is in tune without adjustment
techniques.tempoRule: The fragment is short enough to play at the real tempo. Use it.
techniques.successCriteria: You can enter and leave the measure without a change of pace on either side.
techniques.returnToContext: Play the phrase from the beginning, through the hard measure, into the next phrase's first note.
cautions: PracticeMap chose this technique from the ratings; no source here establishes it.

techniques.title: Play the join into the next idea
techniques.fits: Any phrase that has a following phrase. Practising a phrase to its last note teaches an ending the music does not have.
exclusions: the final phrase, which has nothing to carry into
steps: Play the phrase written, and continue through the first note of the next phrase before stopping.
Notice what the join requires: a bow change, a string crossing, a hand that must already be somewhere else.
Practise only the last two notes of this phrase and the first of the next.
Play the phrase whole again with the join included.
Come back to this join later in the session rather than repeating it now until it is fluent.
listeningGoals: The phrase ending is shaped, not just stopped
The first note of the next idea starts in time
Nothing is rushed in the last bar in anticipation
techniques.tempoRule: The tempo the phrase already works at.
techniques.successCriteria: The join sounds like one continuous line, and you can start it from the phrase's last bar.
techniques.returnToContext: This exercise is the return to context.
cautions: S02 gives limited support for revisiting rather than massing repetitions, in a small study of clarinettists. The overlap rule itself is PracticeMap's.
